content.narrative: Day 6 CFD-MTL results (mem_147) reveal an important architecture-property matching principle: different properties have different architecture and feature completeness requirements. Tg underperformance (44.12 vs 32.31, 36% worse) while Tm (59.93 vs 59.18) and Egc (0.552 vs 0.526) match baseline suggests thermal transition prediction needs deeper architecture or complete features. The MBNN-att paper (mem_146) provides theoretical grounding: intensive properties (Egc) benefit from softmax normalization (attention weights sum to 1), while extensive properties (Tg, Tm) benefit from sigmoid additive contributions (attention weights are independent). Egc's 17% improvement vs Tg's 3% improvement in CFD-MTL aligns with this theory - intensive properties may benefit more from shared learning. The PointGAT paper (mem_145) shows 3D geometry contributes 10.7% for QM properties, suggesting thermal transitions may similarly benefit from conformational features not captured in 2D topology. The Equivariance-Property Matching Principle (mem_148) establishes that periodicity > equivariance > depth for polymer chain properties, but depth still matters - Tg's complex thermal transition physics may require the 5-layer GIN used in baseline, not the simplified 3-layer used in CFD-MTL. This integration establishes clear next steps: deeper GNN for Tg, full 148 features, and property-type-aware attention mechanisms based on MBNN-att findings.

memory.abstract: Property-Type-Aware Attention with Architecture-Depth Matching (PTAA-ADM): Resolve Tg underperformance by combining 5-layer GIN (matching baseline depth), full 148 features, and MBNN-att-inspired property-type-aware attention (softmax for intensive Egc, sigmoid additive for extensive Tg/Tm).

H: H1: Tg underperformance (36% worse than baseline) stems from ARCHITECTURE-DEPTH MISMATCH: 3-layer GIN in CFD-MTL is insufficient for thermal transition physics, while baseline used 5-layer GIN. Thermal transitions involve multi-scale physics (chain stiffness, intermolecular forces, free volume) requiring deeper message-passing.

H2: Property-type-aware attention matters per MBNN-att findings: intensive properties (Egc) benefit from softmax normalization (attention weights sum to 1, ensuring size invariance), while extensive properties (Tg, Tm) benefit from sigmoid additive contributions (attention weights are independent, allowing additive scaling). Egc's 17% improvement vs Tg's 3% in CFD-MTL aligns with this theory.

H3: Feature completeness matters more for thermal transitions than melting or band gap: Tg's dominant feature (rotatable_bond_frac, r=-0.73) captures chain rigidity, which requires more complex multi-scale representation than Egc's conjugation (r=-0.747) or Tm's crystallinity. Full 148 features may contain critical rigidity determinants missing from 80-feature subset.
H4: Combining deeper architecture (5-layer), complete features (148), and property-type-aware attention will resolve Tg underperformance while maintaining Tm/Egc baseline-matching performance.

memory.abstract: Distribution-Validated Pre-training with Ensemble-Guided Curation (DV-PGC): Validate PI1M-Tg distribution alignment via UMAP, use ensemble epistemic uncertainty to identify high-value pre-training samples, pre-train with non-redundant polymer similarity learning (no feature prediction) to avoid Day 3 negative transfer.
memory.keyword: pre-training, distribution validation, ensemble uncertainty, epistemic, non-redundant tasks

H: H1: Day 3 pre-training failure (21.4% degradation) was caused by TWO factors: (a) PI1M distribution not validated against Tg/Tm/Egc distributions (likely mismatch), (b) redundant feature prediction task (teaching already-computed 148-dim features). Addressing BOTH will enable beneficial pre-training.

H2: Distribution validation via UMAP/t-SNE projection is NECESSARY before any pre-training. Coverage ratio < 0.7 or high KL divergence indicates curation is required. Curated subset matching downstream distribution will outperform full PI1M pre-training.

H3: Ensemble epistemic uncertainty from Day 4-5 framework can GUIDE pre-training data curation: high-epistemic samples in Tg/Tm/Egc indicate underrepresented chemical subspaces. Selecting PI1M samples similar to high-epistemic downstream samples will maximize pre-training value.

H4: Non-redundant pre-training tasks are ESSENTIAL: polymer similarity learning (contrastive, structure-based, NO feature prediction) will avoid the redundancy that caused Day 3 failure. GPIP succeeded with non-redundant tasks; PF-CL failed with redundant feature prediction.

X.baseline: Day 3 PF-CL pre-training: Tg 39.23±1.81 (21.4% worse than 32.31 baseline). Full PI1M with joint contrastive + feature prediction.
X.target: Tg < 32.0 (beneficial transfer, beating baseline), with validated distribution alignment and documented pre-training methodology
X.core_innovation: Three-stage controlled pre-training: (1) Distribution validation via UMAP + coverage metrics, (2) Ensemble-guided curation using epistemic uncertainty to select high-value PI1M samples, (3) Non-redundant pre-training (polymer similarity learning only, NO feature prediction).

phase_1_distribution_validation: Step 1.1: Compute molecular fingerprints for PI1M (1M) and Tg/Tm/Egc datasets using same featurization
Step 1.2: Project all datasets to 2D using UMAP (n_neighbors=30, min_dist=0.1)
Step 1.3: Compute distribution overlap metrics: (a) Coverage ratio = fraction of downstream samples within k-NN distance of PI1M, (b) KL divergence between distributions, (c) Centroid distance
Step 1.4: Decision point: If coverage_ratio < 0.7 OR KL_divergence > threshold → CURATE subset
phase_2_ensemble_guided_curation: Step 2.1: Run ensemble on Tg/Tm/Egc to compute epistemic uncertainty (variance of predictive means across seeds)
Step 2.2: Identify high-epistemic samples (top 20%) - these indicate underrepresented chemical subspaces
Step 2.3: For each high-epistemic downstream sample, find k-NN in PI1M (k=10)
Step 2.4: Curate PI1M subset: union of all k-NN sets + random sampling for coverage, target 50K-100K samples
Step 2.5: Validate curated subset has better coverage ratio than full PI1M
phase_3_non_redundant_pretraining: Step 3.1: Pre-training task: Polymer Similarity Learning (contrastive, structure-based)
Step 3.2: Positive pairs: polymers with similar structure (Tanimoto similarity > 0.7 on fingerprints)
Step 3.3: Negative pairs: polymers with dissimilar structure (Tanimoto < 0.3)
Step 3.4: Loss: InfoNCE with temperature τ=0.1, NO feature prediction auxiliary task
Step 3.5: Pre-train on curated PI1M subset for 10-20 epochs
Step 3.6: Fine-tune on Tg, compare to 32.31 baseline

implementation_steps: Step 1: Distribution analysis - UMAP projection of PI1M vs Tg/Tm/Egc, compute coverage metrics
Step 2: Run ensemble on downstream tasks to identify high-epistemic samples
Step 3: Curate PI1M subset using k-NN from high-epistemic samples (target 50K-100K)
Step 4: Implement polymer similarity learning (contrastive, NO feature prediction)
Step 5: Pre-train on curated subset
Step 6: Fine-tune on Tg, compare to baseline
Step 7: If beneficial, extend to Tm/Egc; if negative, document and abort

Y2: If H2 is correct, curated subset will have coverage_ratio > 0.8 (better than full PI1M), enabling beneficial pre-training.
Y3: If H3 is correct, high-epistemic samples will cluster in specific chemical subspaces (visible in UMAP), and curated PI1M samples will cover these subspaces.

failure_modes_and_mitigation: Failure mode 1: PI1M distribution completely disjoint from downstream - no curation can fix. Mitigation: Document finding, focus on multi-task learning (Idea 1) instead.
Failure mode 2: Curated subset too small (< 10K) for effective pre-training. Mitigation: Relax k-NN criteria, accept larger subset with lower precision.
Failure mode 3: Polymer similarity learning still causes negative transfer. Mitigation: Try masked property prediction with pseudo-labels, or abort pre-training direction.
Failure mode 4: Pre-training helps Tg but hurts Tm/Egc. Mitigation: Use property-specific fine-tuning rates or separate pre-training for each property.

memory.abstract: Segment-Level Pre-training via Masked Segment Property Prediction: Pre-train on polymer chains by masking segments and predicting their physical properties from context, teaching chain physics without distribution mismatch or feature redundancy that caused PI1M pre-training failure.
memory.keyword: segment pre-training, chain physics, masked prediction, polymer language model, pre-training objective
memory.content: {"H": ["H1: PI1M pre-training failed (21.4% degradation) because: (a) token-level masking teaches SMILES syntax, not polymer physics; (b) predicting computed features is redundant when features are available at inference; (c) distribution mismatch between PI1M and downstream tasks. Segment-level pre-training addresses all three failures.", "H2: Polymer physics operates at segment level - chain connectivity, stiffness, inter-segment interactions. Segment-level masking forces the model to learn these physics from context, which is non-trivial and non-redundant.", "H3: Segment property prediction from context teaches three chain physics principles: (a) segment-segment correlations (rigid segments cluster), (b) chain stiffness patterns (conjugated segments propagate stiffness), (c) inter-segment interactions (neighboring segments affect each other's properties).", "H4: Pre-training objectives should teach what cannot be computed: context-dependent properties. Segment rigidity in isolation is computable, but segment rigidity in chain context requires understanding chain physics. This is the key to non-redundant pre-training."], "X": {"experiment_name": "Segment-Level Pre-training via Masked Segment Property Prediction (SLP)", "baseline": "No pre-training (Tg: 32.31, Tm: 59.18±1.12, Egc: 0.5262±0.0471); PI1M pre-training (Tg: 39.23, 21.4% degradation)", "core_innovation": "Pre-train on PI1M at segment level (not token level) by masking segments and predicting their physical properties from context segments. This teaches chain physics without distribution mismatch or feature redundancy.", "theoretical_foundation": ["Scale matching: Polymer physics operates at segment level (chain connectivity, stiffness, inter-segment interactions). Token-level masking (TransPolymer, PF-CL) teaches SMILES syntax, not polymer physics.", "Non-redundancy principle: Pre-training should teach non-computable properties. Segment properties in isolation are computable, but segment properties in chain context require understanding chain physics.", "Context-dependent physics: Segment rigidity is affected by neighboring segments (conjugation propagation, steric hindrance, intermolecular forces). Predicting masked segment properties from context forces learning these interactions.", "Distribution universality: Segment physics (connectivity, stiffness) is universal across polymer space, avoiding PI1M-Tg distribution mismatch."], "architecture": ["Segment Tokenizer: Split polymer chain into segments (repeat units). Each segment is a node in segment graph.", "  - Option 1: Each repeat unit is a segment (n segments per polymer)", "  - Option 2: Group repeat units by chemical similarity (variable segment size)", "Segment Encoder: GNN processes segment graph, outputs segment embeddings s_i", "  - Use PerioGT backbone with periodicity encoding", "  - Segment graph: nodes = segments, edges = covalent bonds between segments", "Masked Segment Prediction: Randomly mask 15-20% of segments", "  - For masked segment i, predict: rigidity (rotatable_bond_frac), conjugation (π_electron_density), size (heavy_atom_count)", "  - Prediction head: MLP(s_context) → [rigidity, conjugation, size] where s_context is aggregated from unmasked neighbors", "Context Aggregation: For masked segment i, aggregate information from context segments", "  - Option 1: Mean aggregation of neighbor segment embeddings", "  - Option 2: Attention aggregation (attend to unmasked neighbors)", "  - Option 3: Position-aware aggregation (consider chain position)"], "pre_training_objectives": ["Objective 1: Segment Rigidity Prediction", "  - Target: rotatable_bond_frac of masked segment (computed from segment structure)", "  - Loss: L_rigidity = MSE(predicted_rigidity, computed_rigidity)", "  - Why non-trivial: Rigidity in chain context differs from isolated segment (conjugation propagation, steric hindrance)", "Objective 2: Segment Conjugation Prediction", "  - Target: π_electron_density of masked segment (computed from segment structure)", "  - Loss: L_conjugation = MSE(predicted_conjugation, computed_conjugation)", "  - Why non-trivial: Conjugation extends across segment boundaries, context affects prediction", "Objective 3: Segment Size Prediction", "  - Target: heavy_atom_count of masked segment", "  - Loss: L_size = MSE(predicted_size, computed_size)", "  - Why non-trivial: Chain context constrains segment size (polymers tend toward uniform segments)", "Objective 4: Inter-Segment Distance Prediction (optional)", "  - Target: 3D distance between masked segment and its neighbors (requires conformer)", "  - Loss: L_distance = MSE(predicted_distance, computed_distance)", "  - Why non-trivial: Requires learning chain conformation physics", "Total Pre-training Loss: L_pretrain = λ_1 * L_rigidity + λ_2 * L_conjugation + λ_3 * L_size + λ_4 * L_distance"], "training_paradigm": ["Phase 1: Pre-training on PI1M (1M unlabeled polymers)", "  - Split each polymer into segments", "  - Mask 15-20% of segments per polymer", "  - Predict masked segment properties from context", "  - Train for N epochs until convergence", "Phase 2: Fine-tuning on downstream tasks (Tg, Tm, Egc)", "  - Initialize encoder with pre-trained weights", "  - Add property prediction head (MLP from segment embeddings to property)", "  - Aggregate segment embeddings (mean, attention, or Fermi-Dirac)", "  - Fine-tune on labeled data"], "implementation_details": ["Segment masking strategy:", "  - Random masking: 15-20% of segments randomly selected", "  - Block masking: consecutive segments masked (harder, teaches longer-range dependencies)", "  - Stratified masking: ensure diverse segment types are masked", "Context window: Limit context to k nearest neighbors (k=3-5) to focus on local chain physics", "Prediction targets: Use computed segment properties (not learned), ensuring pre-training teaches physics, not memorization", "Negative sampling: Include 'impossible' segment predictions (segments that don't fit chain context) as negatives"], "key_differences_from_PI1M": ["Scale: Segment-level (polymer physics) vs Token-level (SMILES syntax)", "Objective: Predict context-dependent properties vs Predict redundant computed features", "Distribution: Universal segment physics vs Mismatched polymer distribution", "Non-redundancy: Context-dependent prediction requires learning chain physics vs Isolated feature prediction is trivial"], "ablation_studies": ["Ablation 1: No pre-training (baseline)", "Ablation 2: Token-level pre-training (TransPolymer/PF-CL style) - expect degradation", "Ablation 3: Segment-level pre-training with single objective (rigidity only)", "Ablation 4: Segment-level pre-training with all objectives (rigidity + conjugation + size)", "Ablation 5: Segment-level pre-training with block masking (harder task)", "Ablation 6: Fine-tuning with frozen encoder vs full fine-tuning"], "data_requirements": ["Pre-training: PI1M (1M unlabeled polymers)", "Fine-tuning: Tg (7170), Tm (3651), Egc (3380)", "Segment properties: Computed from segment structure (rotatable_bond_frac, π_electron_density, heavy_atom_count)"], "computational_considerations": ["Pre-training: ~1M polymers, segment-level processing, ~10-20 epochs", "Fine-tuning: Same as baseline (~7K samples, 5-fold CV)", "Memory: Segment graph is smaller than atom graph (fewer nodes, same edges)", "Compute: 2x 2080Ti sufficient for segment-level pre-training"]}, "Y": {"expected_observables": ["Y1: Segment-level pre-training improves downstream Tg/Tm/Egc prediction (lower RMSE than no pre-training), validating H1 that segment-level physics is the right scale for pre-training.", "Y2: Pre-trained encoder learns segment-segment correlations: embedding similarity correlates with segment property similarity (rigid segments cluster in embedding space).", "Y3: Context-dependent prediction is non-trivial: prediction error for masked segment properties is higher than for isolated segments, validating H4 that context-dependent properties require learning chain physics.", "Y4: Pre-training transfer is positive (no degradation like PI1M): fine-tuned models outperform no-pre-training baseline, validating H2 that segment-level pre-training addresses PI1M failures.", "Y5: Block masking (consecutive segments) improves performance more than random masking, showing model learns longer-range chain dependencies."], "success_criteria": {"minimum_acceptable": "Tg RMSE < 32.0 (no degradation, slight improvement over baseline)", "target": "Tg RMSE < 30.0, Tm RMSE < 55.0, Egc RMSE < 0.50 (positive transfer from pre-training)", "stretch": "Tg RMSE < 28.0 (matching or exceeding PI1M-pretrained SOTA without distribution matching)", "scientific_value": "Pre-trained embeddings are interpretable (segment clustering by rigidity, conjugation); pre-training objectives teach chain physics (context-dependent predictions); establishes segment-level as the right scale for polymer pre-training."}, "failure_modes_and_mitigation": ["Failure mode 1: Segment property prediction is too easy (trivial from local segment features). Mitigation: Use block masking, increase masking ratio, predict context-dependent properties (inter-segment distance).", "Failure mode 2: Pre-training doesn't transfer to downstream tasks. Mitigation: Analyze embedding space (UMAP), check if pre-trained features correlate with downstream property determinants.", "Failure mode 3: Distribution mismatch persists (PI1M vs downstream). Mitigation: Filter PI1M to match downstream distribution, or use curriculum learning (easy polymers first).", "Failure mode 4: Pre-training is computationally expensive. Mitigation: Use smaller PI1M subset, early stopping, or distillation.", "Failure mode 5: Fine-tuning overwrites pre-trained knowledge. Mitigation: Use lower learning rate for encoder, gradual unfreezing, or adapter layers."], "connection_to_existing_knowledge": ["Addresses PI1M pre-training failure (mem_001): segment-level avoids distribution mismatch, context-dependent prediction avoids feature redundancy", "Leverages PerioGT periodicity encoding (mem_075): segment graph naturally encodes chain periodicity", "Incorporates Feature-First Principle (mem_095): pre-training teaches physics-informed segment properties (rigidity, conjugation)", "Extends TransPolymer (mem_039): segment-level masking vs token-level masking, property prediction vs language modeling", "Different from PF-CL (mem_105): PF-CL predicted 148-dim features (redundant), SLP predicts context-dependent properties (non-redundant)"], "why_conceptually_distant": ["Current polymer pre-training (TransPolymer, PF-CL) operates at token level, teaching SMILES syntax. SLP operates at segment level, teaching polymer physics.", "Current pre-training objectives predict features that are computed and available at inference (redundant). SLP predicts context-dependent properties that require understanding chain physics (non-redundant).", "Current pre-training failed due to distribution mismatch (PI1M vs downstream). SLP uses universal segment physics that transfers across polymer distributions.", "Current pre-training treats polymer as sequence of tokens. SLP treats polymer as chain of interacting segments, matching the scale of polymer physics.", "This is the first pre-training approach designed for polymer physics (not NLP adaptation), addressing all three failure modes of PI1M pre-training: scale mismatch, feature redundancy, distribution mismatch."]}
